I am pleased to share our recent publication, authored by Hao Gao , our former co-op student, marking his first paper as the lead author. He developed an innovative methodology for monitoring LME crack progression during spot welding. Hao trained custom YOLOv9 models and integrated them with the simple online and real-time tracking (SORT) system to enable accurate tracking and measurement of multiple LME cracks. The trained models achieved mAP@50 scores of 0.920 and 0.921, demonstrating that this approach significantly reduces the time required for manual crack tracking. The paper is now available; you can access it via the link below. 👉 https://lnkd.in/gEaztaqP This research is supported by the Auto/Steel Partnership (A/SP), so I would like to extend special thanks to Hassan Ghassemi-Armaki , Eric McCarty , and Kevin (Zhenke) Teng . Congratulations on your first paper, Hao Gao 👏. I also appreciate the contributions of co-authors: Reza Bakhtiari, Ph.D. , Ali Afzal, Hasan Habib , Ahmad Aminzadeh. PhD , and our supervisor, Elliot Biro .

I'm recruiting 2–4 Georgia Tech students to help me build the world's first RC aircraft to break Mach 1. Last month my 500mph Reaper build went viral (5M+ views, and a "Nice" from Elon Musk). Blake Scholl , CEO of Boom Supersonic , announced the Boom Prize in direct response to my post: a prize given to the first amateur team to fly a remotely piloted, air-breathing aircraft past Mach 1. Selection is purely on what you've built. I don't care about GPA, major, or year. Demonstrate hardware experience, CAD, code, flight videos etc. The team will be kept lean, small enough to move fast and avoid bloat. Expect real hours and real hardware. First flight is targeted for Nov/Dec 2026. Apply here, form closes on Aug 23: https://lnkd.in/gDmtr-a6

As I close a successful chapter at 1X , I’ve been reflecting on how much this experience has shaped me as an engineer. My journey at 1X started with an internship, and I later had the chance to return as a full-time Mechanical Engineer, where I was able to contribute to exciting and challenging work in humanoid robotics. From turning early ideas into physical prototypes to designing, building, testing, and improving hardware alongside a talented team, every project gave me something new to learn. This experience also reinforced what I enjoy most about engineering: taking a problem that may not yet have a clear solution and turning an idea into something physical that can be tested, learned from, and improved. Along the way, I learned the importance of moving quickly while remaining thoughtful, adapting when the path isn’t obvious, and working closely across disciplines to bring ideas into the real world. More than anything, I’m thankful to the people who supported me, trusted me, challenged my thinking, and made this chapter so memorable. It has been a privilege to contribute to 1X’s mission and to learn from so many talented people along the way. I’m grateful for everything this experience taught me. Thank you, 1X . More on what’s next soon.

Crusoe and Aalo Atomics form strategic partnership with goal of deploying first nuclear-powered AI factory. DENVER, Colorado and AUSTIN, Texas, July 30, 2026 – Crusoe , the industry’s first vertically integrated AI infrastructure provider, and Aalo Atomics , the company building fully modular nuclear plants (XMRs) to power modern AI data centers, today announce a strategic partnership focused on developing and deploying the first nuclear-powered AI Factory data center designed to validate nuclear power’s effectiveness with AI workloads. “The next generation of AI infrastructure demands power that is reliable, abundant,clean and at scale, and Aalo’s nuclear reactors are built to meet that need,” said Cully Cavness, Co-Founder, President and Chief Strategy Officer, Crusoe. “One of Crusoe’s core values is to ‘bend the arc of energy toward sustainability,’ and within that value we embrace the principle of using Crusoe’s market position to support and accelerate energy innovation. In line with our core values, we look forward to Aalo and Crusoe jointly demonstrating to the industry the first AI data center powered by a small modular nuclear reactor." Aalo will initially power a Crusoe Spark ™ modular data center, running Crusoe Cloud, in 2027 at Idaho National Laboratory as a proof of concept. Looking forward, Aalo and Crusoe intend to deploy Aalo Pods, Aalo’s 50 MWe XMR power plants at Crusoe data centers, by the end of 2029. “As one of only four companies to reach criticality by President Trump’s deadline for companies in the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, we are now well positioned for not only the full power operation of our 10 MWe Aalo-X reactor, but also the deployment of the Aalo Pod to power commercial data centers,” said Matt Loszak, CEO, Aalo Atomics. “We are now the only nuclear technology company to design and build a nuclear reactor fueled to produce 10MW of electricity– an achievement that positions Aalo as the premier power provider for the modern data center.” Aalo has already begun work on its second nuclear reactor, testing a commercial-scale system that will produce electricity and power for an on-site Crusoe Spark modular data center. About Crusoe As the AI factory company, Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. The company provides a reliable, scalable, cost-effective, energy-first solution for AI infrastructure. By harnessing large-scale energy sources, building AI-optimized data centers, and delivering a powerful AI cloud platform, Crusoe empowers its customers and partners to build the future faster. About Aalo Atomics Aalo Atomics designs and builds factory-manufactured nuclear power plants for data centers, industry, and cities. AI infrastructure requires firm, high-density power on timelines the existing grid cannot support. The Aalo Pod delivers it as a complete modular power plant, mass-manufactured in a factory and sited directly at the load.
